Build up over a run-in zone, then hold maximum velocity through a ten-yard timed zone before decelerating gradually. Full recovery between every rep.

name: Catch and Shoot off the Hop

instructions.overview: Move into the catch, hop into a squared-up stance as the ball arrives, and rise straight into the shot without an extra step. Repeat from multiple spots.

Push vertically at full speed, then sink the hips and break back toward the quarterback, working back to the ball rather than waiting for it.
Attack a line of cones, executing a different handle at each one - crossover, between the legs, behind the back - at game speed with the head up.
Backpedal, break at forty-five degrees, plant and backpedal again in a W pattern down the field, keeping the shoulders over the toes throughout.
Drive the near shoulder under the blocker's arm and rip upward through the gap, finishing with the hips turned and the feet still driving.
Attack the blocker's edge, clear the near arm and bring the far arm over the top in one motion, turning the corner flat to the quarterback.
Play one pass away in a denial stance with the hand in the passing lane, sliding to stay attached as the offensive player moves. Never turn the head away from the ball.

Attack the middle of the lane and release a one-foot floater over an imaginary shot blocker, high off the fingertips with soft touch. Vary the release point.
Beat a press defender off the line using a hard fake and a release to either side, then accelerate downfield in a straight line to the returner.
Slide from the wing into help position at the nail, then recover back out to the shooter on the pass. Repeat until the recovery stays under control.
Dribble forward, rise slightly and pause to freeze the defender, then explode past off the same foot. The change of pace, not the handle, is the point.
Take a short read step on the snap, diagnose the play, then shuffle downhill to the gap without crossing the feet or over-running the ball.
Sprint to a spot ahead of the ball carrier rather than at them, closing the angle and breaking down under control before contact.
Secure a rebound, pivot away from pressure and make a strong outlet pass, then sprint to fill the lane. Ties rebounding to transition offense.
From a pass set, kick the outside foot back and slide to mirror the rusher without crossing the feet, keeping the hands inside and the hips down.
Come off the screen and read the defender's coverage - reject, split, pull up, or hit the roll. Run the same action against each coverage so the read becomes automatic.
Catch with the back to the basket, feel the defender, then drop step baseline and finish strong off two feet. Work both shoulders.
Against a wall pad or partner, use a quick hand swipe and hip turn to escape the press and get back onto the release path. Keep the feet moving through the contact.
Attack with two hard dribbles, gather, and rise into a balanced jump shot with the feet under the shoulders. Work both directions off each hand.
Open with the play-side foot, pull flat down the line and turn up through the hole square to the target. Speed out of the stance is what makes the block.
Track a high ball with defenders closing, catch it cleanly above the numbers and immediately secure it before turning upfield. Never take the eyes off the ball early.
Execute a five-step drop with a controlled hitch at the top, keeping the shoulders square and the ball at chest height throughout the drop.
Run the stem of the route at full speed, sink the hips at the break point and cut sharply without gearing down early. Run the full route tree over the session.
Sell a shot fake with the eyes and the ball, then rip through low and drive past on the first step. The fake must look identical to the real shot.
Move through five perimeter spots making a set number at each before advancing. Square the feet to the rim on the catch at every spot rather than drifting.
Push the ball in transition, then rise into a balanced pull-up jumper at the elbow rather than driving all the way in. Decision speed is the point.

Slide from one side of the free-throw lane to the other in a low stance without crossing the feet, touching the line each time before changing direction.

Travel sideways down the ladder stepping both feet in and both feet out of each square. Face the same direction the whole way, then return leading with the other foot.

Shuffle laterally in a low stance, then on the signal plant and break forward at a forty-five degree angle at full speed. Alternate the breaking direction.

Backpedal several yards under control, then flip the hips and sprint forward at full speed. Work the turn to both the left and the right.

Set up in a balanced two-point stance with the feet staggered and the weight forward, then explode out for three hard steps on the go signal. Reset and repeat.
Jog forward carrying the ball high and tight while swinging the free arm to fend off imaginary defenders, switching the carry arm halfway. Never let the ball drop below the elbow.
Step into a wide stance and push the ball through the legs from front hand to back hand. Keep the dribble low and the head up, and alternate lead legs.
From a defensive stance, turn and pivot into an imaginary opponent, sitting the hips back with wide elbows to seal them out, then explode up for the rebound.
From an athletic stance, snap the ball low and hard across the body from one hand to the other, keeping it below the knees. Shift the weight with the ball each time.
Without dribbling, weave the ball in a figure-8 pattern through and around the legs, passing it hand to hand. Start slow for control, then build speed.
Stand a few feet from the rim and shoot one-handed with the guide hand off the ball, focusing on elbow alignment and a held follow-through. Make a set number before stepping back.
Start directly under the rim and make a set number of one-handed form shots, then step back one stride at a time, resetting the count at each distance. Any miss returns the athlete one step closer.
Shoot free throws using the exact same pre-shot routine every attempt - same dribble count, same breath, same release. Consistency of the routine is the drill, not the make percentage.
Receive or pick up the ball on the move, jump stop onto two feet, then execute a front pivot and a reverse pivot without traveling. Emphasize the still, balanced landing.
Attack the rim from the wing at controlled speed, gathering on the outside foot and finishing high off the backboard. Complete reps from both sides of the floor.
Alternate short layups on either side of the rim, catching the ball out of the net and going straight back up with the opposite hand. Stay under control and use the backboard every time.

Drive baseline and finish on the far side of the rim, using the backboard as protection from the help defender. Complete reps from both sides.
Release off the line, take three hard steps and break flat across the field at a sharp angle without rounding the cut. Catch with the hands away from the body.
After an imaginary pass out of the paint, relocate along the arc to a new spot and square up ready to shoot. Move on every rep rather than standing still.
Set the position-specific stance, hold it, then explode into the first three steps of the assigned technique on the snap count. Reset fully every rep.
Dribble the ball hard into the floor at knee height with one hand, keeping the eyes up and off the ball. Complete the set on one hand, then switch. Attack the ball rather than patting it.
Set the feet, sink the hips, and place one hand on the ground with the weight balanced rather than leaning. Hold the stance, then fire out low on the count.
Grip the ball with the fingers on the laces, step toward the target, rotate the hips through and finish with the throwing hand across the opposite hip. Focus on the whole sequence, not on distance.
Stand a few feet from a solid wall and chest-pass the ball into it, catching and releasing as fast as possible without letting the ball settle. Keep the elbows in and the feet set.
